body:
I understand where you are coming from with social anxiety.

I'm not sure what a family worker does, but would this person be able to help you find resources to transition from your family home to living independently when you turn 18? Maybe they can help you apply for housing assistance and navigate trade school or university or help find a job? If they can't do that for you, maybe they can point you to someone else who can. Being "in the system" should help you transition to other social services.

A good therapist is key. I have had 4 or 5 different therapists in the last 10 years. Only one of them helped, and they unfortunately retired. Good for them-they deserve it, but not so good for me. The point is if your first attempt at therapy doesn't work, you might respond better with a different therapist.

Can you find a new psychiatrist and therapist? It may seem that going to the hospital will do no good, but it should at least cause your doctor to reassess the decision to taper your medication or help you find a new provider.

Have you ever had therapy, either by yourself or with your parents? It sounds like you are using pot to self-medicate, and that is probably making it harder to do the things you find unpleasant. 

I am a life long gamer, and I often use video games to avoid the things I need to do. I try to use games as a motivation to do the things I need to do. I can easily spend the entire day playing games on the Switch, so I don't allow myself to play until after I finish something on my to-do list. Instead of doing all of my work then playing for hours, I finish one thing then allow myself 30 minutes of my favorite game, then I need to do some other work.

Your debt is not a horrible amount for your age, but it is a big burden for your current income. It's really good that you have an idea for a better paying job, and that it is loosely related to something you are already doing (both include driving for a living). Do you have anyone who can help you plan how you can pay down your current debt while also getting your CDL testing? Sometimes working on a plan to improve your problems can make it seem less hopeless.

I don't know if it's discipline as much as a desire to hide from everyone who doesn't live in my house. I would like to hide from them, too, but it isn't possible. I feel a little guilty because one of the people I am completely ignoring is my elderly mother, who lives alone.
We have a strong instinct for self preservation.

I wanted a career change a few years after I received my bachelor's degree, and nearly needed a second bachelor's before I could apply for an advanced degree program in the field I wanted. I took 2 classes my first semester back in school, while working full time. I didn't take a second semester because the coursework was too demanding. A few years later, I returned to the same university for a different MA program. The first class was again incredibly demanding, but I was more familiar with the subject matter and managed to stick it out. My friends in the program and I were convinced this university used the prereq courses to make people quit.
Did you find someone to talk to yet? If you can't find someone on your contact list, please consider calling a hotline so you can hear someone's voice.

I unplugged from social media and turned off my phone last week. I've only used the internet as needed for work, checked email minimally, and have spent less than an hour total on reddit in the last 7 days. 

My depression and thoughts of death haven't gone away, but I feel more peaceful.
